title: Record-keeping vocabulary -- what a place may hold, who may write it, how it ages (ADR-015 amendment 8)
description: The one home of the words a RECORDS MAP is written in. The layout declaration (`layout` schema) names every place a host has; each of its entries says what KIND of truth lives there (`holds`), WHO may write it (`writer`) and how it AGES (`lifecycle`), and every one of those words is a row of this document -- never an `enum` in a schema and never a list inside an interpreter. The field anchor is records management (ISO 15489: a record has a declared home, an accountable writer and a disposition) read through information architecture. OPEN BY CONSTRUCTION (Cardinal II): this schema constrains the SHAPE of a row, never the set of rows; a new kind, writer or lifecycle is a new row, and the gate that resolves the map against this document (`FF-RECORDS-DECLARED`) is not touched.

kinds.description: What a place HOLDS: the kind of truth living there, stated so that a document of another kind found in that place is recognisably misfiled.

writers.description: WHO may write a place: an accountable authority, named by what it is accountable FOR, never by a runtime product or a host's role name.

lifecycles.description: How a place's content AGES and where it goes when it is no longer current -- its disposition, in ISO 15489's sense.
